text:
incident-bot: [P0] serving-runtime: GPU container crash on gpu-prod-12 — CUDA illegal memory access detected. Auto-escalation to on-call. Stack excerpt attached.

incident-bot: node: gpu-prod-12, pods impacted: rtx-serve-3 (model: gpt-large-v2), rtx-serve-4 (model: reranker-v1), start: 2026-03-15T01:03:09Z

David-oncall: I'm on it. seeing alerts for 503s and increased tail latency from customers routing through region-us-west. Can someone paste the OOM/CUDA log?

Alice-sre: logs from rtx-serve-3: 
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda_driver.cc:... CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: a device-side assert was triggered
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  cuda kernel failed: misaligned address in gemm_op.cu:453
GPU0: SM 80, L2 errors: 12, Page faults: 0
Pid 23412: signal 11 (SIGSEGV), crashing thread tid 23440
```

Ben-mlinfra: That's consistent with a misaligned pointer in the fused attention kernel we've been dogfooding. We pushed a micro-optim change to layout last week (commit 0a1b2c3) — rolling that back might be fastest fix.

Carla-support: Customers reporting 502/503 from the API gateway. Minimal SLO alerts from 02:00-02:05 UTC, a handful of high-priority orgs flagged. Keeping them updated.

David-oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) mark gpu-prod-12 unschedulable, 2) drain pods (so autoscaler can recreate on other nodes), 3) rollback the kernel layout change on runtime host pool if quick, 4) fallback route traffic to dedicated-1. Ben, can you advise on rollback risk?

Ben-mlinfra: Rolling back runtime kernel/layout patch is low-risk; it's a code path change in our CUDA kernels. It will require draining the pool to avoid mixed-kernel execution. ETA for build + deploy: ~18-22 minutes if we build a hotpatch container. If we can't wait, we can force-routing to variant-model (gpt-large-v2-quantized) that uses a different code path.

Evan-ctrlexec: Starting drain of gpu-prod-12 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-prod-12 && kubectl drain gpu-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — pods are terminating. Noting some stateful pods (vectordb) pinned; they might need manual evict.

Alice-sre: Eviction logs show rtx-serve-3 failed to restart on other nodes due to image pull limit on dedicated pool. I'm opening a ticket to scale image-puller DaemonSet.

Carla-support: Update for customers: "We are observing GPU node crashes causing degraded inference availability in US-WEST. Engineers are actively mitigating. We'll share ETA within 30m." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

David-oncall: Running `kubectl logs rtx-serve-3 -n serving --previous` shows repeated kernel stack. Also seeing `nvmlDeviceGetInvocationType` spurious errors, might be driver-related. What driver version?

Ben-mlinfra: Drivers on prod nodes: NVIDIA 535.54.03, runtime compiled against cudnn 9.2. We haven't upgraded drivers recently. The change in commit 0a1b2c3 rearranged shared memory alignment in fused_gemm. The alignment bug only shows up under long sequence lengths or highly packed KV cache. Likely race with KV cache invalidation on reload.

Alice-sre: I see a pattern: crashes spike during model hot reloads (we load new weights while the node still serves). There's a short window where kernel kernel-launch config might still use old pointers. I'll push an immediate guard in the loader to stop concurrent kernel launches during weight swap. Quick patch to the loader is ~8-10m to build and can be canaryed.

Ben-mlinfra: That's good. Two parallel mitigations: 1) patch loader to serialized reloads (quick), 2) hotpatch kernel rollback (longer). I'll start building the hotpatch but can we canary the loader patch to dedicated-2?

Evan-ctrlexec: Canary deploy to dedicated-2 started. `kubectl set image deployment/serving-loader loader=redwood/serving-loader:canary-20260315 && kubectl rollout status deploy/serving-loader -n serving` — canary is up on 2 pods. No crashes in the 2m window so far.

Carla-support: Customers updated: "We've deployed a mitigation and are confirming improved stability in the affected region. We're monitoring and will post further updates."

David-oncall: Monitoring metrics: error rate for text-generation routes dropped from 8% -> 1.2% after drain + canary. Some residual traffic still hitting older replicas in staging - TTL for LB caches may take a minute.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledgment recorded by David-oncall at 2026-03-15T01:06:14Z

Alice-sre: Quick patch diff I applied to loader (canary): added `std::atomic_bool reloading` check around weight swap, and `synchronise_streams()` before freeing old pointers. This prevents concurrent kernel launches touching freed memory.

Ben-mlinfra: If loader guard holds, crash surface should be gone, but it's a bandaid for the kernel bug. Recommend follow-up: revert commit 0a1b2c3 and write unit/regression test for alignment under heavy KV concurrency. Also file ticket to audit all fused kernels for unaligned access.

Evan-ctrlexec: gpu-prod-12 drained and cordoned successfully. No new crashes since canary. Draining freed up rtx-serve-3 which restarted on gpu-prod-21 fine.

Carla-support: Impact summary for event timeline (customer-facing):
- Detection: 2026-03-15T01:03 UTC
- Mitigation: drains + loader canary deployed by 01:14 UTC
- Partial recovery: error rates back to baseline by 01:21 UTC
- Impact: transient 5-10m of 502/503s for ~3% of requests in US-WEST, a few high-priority customers saw degraded throughput.

David-oncall: I'm going to hand off long-term remediation to Ben and Alice. I'll keep incident in "monitoring" for 2h then close if stable. Ben/Alice set follow-up issues and assign owners.

Ben-mlinfra: Creating follow-up GitHub issue: "misaligned-access: rollback layout change + kernel audit" and adding reproducer steps. Tagging infra-repro and test-team.

Alice-sre: I'll push a commit to ensure model hot-reloads use the serialized loader by default and add a stress test to CI for concurrent reloads.

Carla-support: I'll send a post-incident note to affected customers with the timeline and mitigation details.

David-oncall: Thanks team. I'll mark pagerduty as resolved after observation window. Closing notes: root cause likely race during weight hot-swap exposing alignment bug in fused_gemm kernel. Live mitigation: drain, canary serialized-loader, and plan rollback. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident updated to MONITORING. Postmortem owner: alice-sre.

Evan-ctrlexec: leaving channel, assigning follow-ups in ticket tracker.

Carla-support: adding affected orgs list to the ticket.

David-oncall: last check 01:29 UTC — metrics stable. I'll close thread at 01:36 if no regressions.

(reacts: david-oncall :thumbsup:, alice-sre :rocket:)
